requirement_text.REQ-373:
Filed from a GUI-review sweep applying "review real screens before writing a blind Playwright spec" to test/fixtures/uat/scenarios/platform/instance-pin-survives-catalog-change.yaml (test/uat-reports/gui-review-2026-09-20-instance-pin-survives-catalog-change.md has the full trace). That scenario's own stale NOTE (ISS-0527) already flagged its pipeline_test as an aspirational forward-reference to a feature never built; this run verified that independently by reading current source rather than trusting the note, and confirms the underlying feature genuinely does not exist, in whole or in part.

WHAT EXISTS TODAY, verified 2026-09-20 by direct source read (not inference): Letflow.Engine.PinResolver (REQ-059, PIN-01..04) and Letflow.Engine.PinResolver's PIN-05 explicit-rebind sibling (REQ-060) implement the full event-sourced MACHINERY this scenario's steps exercise -- freezing every versioned catalog_entry/module/variable_schema dependency into the INSTANCE_STARTED event payload at case-start time (never re-read live), replay-deriving the effective pin set purely from already-appended events (reconstruct_effective_pins/2, zero catalog reads by construction), child-instance inheritance with conflict recording, and a real, already-shipped PIN-05 rebind path that appends exactly one INSTANCE_PINS_REBOUND event carrying ref/prior_version/new_version/actor/reason per changed entry, atomically, all-or-nothing. This is confirmed real, tested, and RELEASED machinery, not a stub.

What does NOT exist: pin_resolver.ex's own moduledoc states this SCOPE GAP explicitly and by name ("service_catalog (S6) and PLC-01 (unscoped) are not built") -- confirmed still true by reading lib/letflow/service_catalog.ex and lib/letflow/service_catalog/entry.ex in full. The service_catalog table (REQ-191/REQ-192, both done) has NO version or status column whatsoever -- service_id is the table's own primary key, one row per service, with no concept of "a version of this connection" at all. There is therefore no way to publish a second version of a shared connection, no way to retire an old version, and no real Letflow.Engine.PinResolver.Lookup implementation anywhere in the shipped codebase (only Letflow.ServiceCatalog.scope_validator_lookup/1, which builds a DIFFERENT Lookup type -- ServiceScopeValidator.Lookup, for global/tenant scope comparison, not PinResolver.Lookup). Every call to PinResolver.resolve/4 in Engine.create/2 today runs against PinResolver.default_lookup/0, whose catalog_lookup/module_lookup always return {:error, :not_found} -- meaning a real, currently-shipped case can never actually record a resolved catalog_entry pin at all today; only variable_schema pins and caller-supplied overrides are exercised in production. web/src has zero screen showing, for any case, the list of dependency versions it is using and how each was chosen (auto/explicit/inherited) -- grepped in full, no hits beyond unrelated word matches.

THIS REQUIREMENT (backend half, matching REQ-372's precedent of splitting backend-then-frontend across two requirements): (1) add a version identity and a status (at minimum ACTIVE/RETIRED) to service_catalog entries -- decide and record explicitly whether this is a new version-scoped table (service_id + version as a composite key, service_catalog's current row becoming "the currently-resolvable version" pointer) or an in-place status column plus a new sibling table for prior versions; either is acceptable if the decision and its reasoning are stated in the moduledoc, not left implicit; (2) a publish operation that creates a new version without disturbing any already-pinned reference to the prior one; (3) a retire operation that stops the retired version from being chosen by any NEW resolution while leaving it fully resolvable for PinResolver.pin_for/3 reads against an already-pinned instance (PIN-03 AC3's own SCOPE GAP, named in pin_resolver.ex, is exactly what this closes); (4) a real Letflow.Engine.PinResolver.Lookup implementation backed by this versioned catalog, wired into Engine.create/2's pin_lookup/2 helper in place of default_lookup/0 for catalog_entry references (module_ref resolution against PLC-01 remains out of scope -- PLC-01 does not exist in this codebase at all and is unscoped to any stage; do not attempt to build it here). Route/permission surface for publish/retire reuses SVC-04's already-shipped :AdminServicesManage policy (Letflow.Api.Authorization) -- do not invent a new permission name.

SCOPE FENCE: backend version/status lifecycle, the real PinResolver.Lookup wiring, and the publish/retire routes. Does not build the frontend case-detail version-with-provenance screen -- that is explicitly a follow-on FRONTEND-DEV requirement once this lands, filed the same way REQ-291 followed REQ-288 (must show, per EO-003, each dependency's version and whether it was chosen automatically, requested explicitly, or inherited -- Letflow.Engine.PinResolver already returns a `source` field with exactly this taxonomy (:resolved/:override/:inherited/:rebound), so that screen is a read of already-shipped data once a route exposes it -- PIN-04 AC4's own SCOPE note already names GET /api/v1/instances/{id}/pins as the future route). Does not build PLC-01 (module_ref/sub-process catalog versioning) -- that stays the identical, already-named SCOPE GAP pin_resolver.ex's own moduledoc states, unscoped to any stage.

task.description:
Produce the design artefact for REQ-373 at lib/letflow/design/req373-service-catalog-version-lifecycle.md (or your own better name under that directory, your call) per WF-02 Step 1's procedure (docs/agents/workflows/WF-02_requirement_implementation.md). You are on branch feature/WF02-REQ373-20260921 -- verify with `git branch --show-current` before writing anything; STOP and report FAIL if it isn't that. This is a BACKEND-ONLY requirement: design only lib/letflow/ + priv/repo/migrations/ + route changes. No web/ presentation layer -- that is an explicit follow-on FRONTEND-DEV requirement you must NOT design here.

Before designing, RE-VERIFY by reading actual current source (do not trust the requirement text's own claims as final): (a) lib/letflow/service_catalog.ex and lib/letflow/service_catalog/entry.ex in full -- confirm the current schema truly has no version/status column and understand every existing public function's contract, since you must not break any existing caller; (b) lib/letflow/engine/pin_resolver.ex in full -- confirm the PinResolver.Lookup behaviour's exact callback contract (what catalog_lookup/module_lookup must return, the {:resolved,...}/{:override,...}/{:inherited,...}/{:rebound,...} source taxonomy, PIN-03/PIN-04/PIN-05's exact semantics), and confirm default_lookup/0's current {:error,:not_found} stub shape; (c) lib/letflow/engine.ex's create/2 and its pin_lookup/2 helper -- read the exact current call site you must change; (d) lib/letflow_web/router.ex and whatever existing service_catalog admin routes exist (REQ-191/192, SVC-04) -- confirm the exact :AdminServicesManage permission plug/policy shape so you reuse it correctly, not reinvent it; (e) grep docs/migration/decisions/ for any prior decision bearing on versioned-entity schema shape (composite key vs. status+sibling table) so you don't contradict a standing decision record.

Design must cover, explicitly: (1) THE SCHEMA DECISION -- composite-key-versioned-table (service_id+version primary key) vs. status column + sibling table for prior versions. Pick one, state the reasoning in the design (this reasoning must also land in ELIXIR-DEV's shipped moduledoc verbatim in substance), and be explicit about how existing service_catalog rows migrate into the new shape without breaking any existing caller of service_catalog.ex's current public functions (every current caller must keep working, or you must name every call site that needs updating). (2) PUBLISH operation: full @spec-style signature, what it creates (a new version row, ACTIVE), what it explicitly does NOT touch (must not alter any already-recorded INSTANCE_STARTED pin payload -- pins are frozen at case-start and never re-read live, per PinResolver's existing design; state this invariant explicitly so ELIXIR-DEV doesn't accidentally couple publish to any pin-mutation). (3) RETIRE operation: full signature; state EXPLICITLY (not left ambiguous, per the requirement's own AC4 wording) whether a retired version's resolve/4 call fails outright or falls through to the current ACTIVE version -- pick one and justify it -- while explicitly preserving PinResolver.pin_for/3 reads against an already-pinned instance with zero error (name exactly why pin_for/3 is unaffected by retire, given pins never re-read the catalog). (4) THE REAL PinResolver.Lookup IMPLEMENTATION: a new module (your naming call) implementing the Lookup behaviour's catalog_lookup/module_lookup callbacks backed by the versioned catalog -- module_lookup must remain out of scope / return :not_found or equivalent for PLC-01 (do not build module_ref resolution; state this explicitly). (5) THE Engine.create/2 WIRING: exact call-site change replacing PinResolver.default_lookup/0 with the new Lookup for catalog_entry references only -- specify precisely how variable_schema/module_ref pin_lookup/2 behavior is preserved unchanged. (6) ROUTES: publish/retire HTTP routes (method+path, your call, follow existing service_catalog admin route conventions) gated by the EXISTING :AdminServicesManage permission -- do not invent a new permission atom; cite the exact existing plug/policy check by name. (7) Migration spec: table(s), columns, types, constraints, indexes, in full detail -- no 'TBD'.

Every one of REQ-373's 8 acceptance criteria (given in task.acceptance_criteria below) must map to a concrete design element -- state the mapping explicitly in a dedicated design-doc section, one row per AC. List open questions explicitly rather than silently resolving them by guessing. Design artefact only -- @spec-style signatures and type/data shapes, NEVER literal function bodies/case-do-end blocks/literal clause implementations (CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR fails on sight for this, see WF-02 Step 1b check 2e and the REQ-372 precedent in handoffs/WF02-REQ372-20260921/step-01-code-designer.json's rework note for exactly what 'design code, not implementation code' means in practice on this project -- read that rework note before writing, it is instructive).

REWORK ITERATION 1: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (step-01b) FAILed this design on ONE dimension only -- everything else (all 8 ACs mapped, no literal implementation code, the schema-decision reasoning re-verified against service_catalog.ex/entry.ex, AC4's retire-vs-fallback resolution re-verified against pin_resolver.ex's actual pin_for/3, PinResolver.Lookup's real struct-not-behaviour contract, and :AdminServicesManage route/permission reuse re-verified against authorization.ex) was independently re-checked against source and confirmed sound -- do not redo any of that. The single defect: the new `status` field's Ecto representation is internally self-contradictory. Section 4's migration fixes UPPERCASE DB values/CHECK constraint ('ACTIVE'/'RETIRED', matching this codebase's own required_auth Ecto.Enum convention where an atom's casing becomes the DB string verbatim), while Section 3.2 and Section 5's behavior prose repeatedly pattern-matches LOWERCASE atoms (:active/:retired, e.g. 'status = :retired', 'row with status: :active ->'). The design never declares whether `status` is Ecto.Enum, and never states a `values:` mapping reconciling the two casings -- unlike §0's bullet list, which explicitly tags required_auth/scope as '(Ecto.Enum)' but conspicuously omits that tag for status. Fix, narrowly: pick ONE casing convention -- either plain `Ecto.Enum, values: [:ACTIVE, :RETIRED]` (aligning with required_auth's own uppercase-atom convention, so Elixir call sites also use :ACTIVE/:RETIRED), or an explicit `values: [active: "ACTIVE", retired: "RETIRED"]` mapping if lowercase Elixir-side atoms are intentionally preferred -- then make every status literal in §0, §3.2, §4, §5, and §8 consistent with that single choice. Do not touch any other section's content beyond what this reconciliation requires. This is rework iteration 1 of max_rework 3. On completion, set this handoff's status to COMPLETED and result to a genuine first-hand PASS/FAIL report as normal.
acceptance_criteria: service_catalog entries carry a version identity and an ACTIVE/RETIRED status, with the chosen schema (composite key vs. status+sibling table) stated explicitly in the moduledoc along with the reasoning, proven by a migration and a schema test

publishing a new version of an existing service_id does not alter or invalidate any already-resolved pinned_version entry recorded in a prior INSTANCE_STARTED event, proven by a test that resolves a pin, publishes a new version, and re-derives the same instance's effective pin set unchanged
a new case created after a publish resolves the newly published version via Letflow.Engine.PinResolver.resolve/4's real (non-default) Lookup, proven by a test

retiring a version prevents any NEW resolution from choosing it (a fresh resolve/4 call against the retired ref fails or falls through to the current version, whichever this requirement's own design specifies -- stated explicitly, not left ambiguous) while an instance already pinned to the retired version continues to resolve via pin_for/3 with no error, proven by a test covering both sides

Engine.create/2's pin_lookup/2 helper is wired to the real catalog-backed Lookup for catalog_entry references in place of PinResolver.default_lookup/0, proven by an integration test that starts a real instance referencing a SERVICE_TASK's service_id and confirms a :resolved (not :unresolved_catalog_ref-failing) pin is recorded
publish/retire operations are gated behind the already-shipped :AdminServicesManage permission (Letflow.Api.Authorization), not a newly invented permission name, proven by a test

PLC-01/module_ref catalog versioning is explicitly named as still out of scope in the moduledoc, with a citation of pin_resolver.ex's own existing SCOPE GAP language, not silently expanded into this requirement's scope
mix letflow.check passes, with real output quoted

result.summary:
REWORK ITERATION 1 fix only: resolved the status-field casing self-contradiction CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR flagged. Picked plain `Ecto.Enum, values: [:ACTIVE, :RETIRED]` (uppercase Elixir-side atoms, matching this codebase's own required_auth convention, not scope's lowercase one) so the atom serializes to the DB string verbatim with no values: remapping -- consistent with §4's migration, which was already correct (CHECK (status IN ('ACTIVE','RETIRED')), default 'ACTIVE'). Added an explicit new subsection to §3.3 stating the Entry schema field declaration (`field(:status, Ecto.Enum, values: [:ACTIVE, :RETIRED], default: :ACTIVE)`) and the casing rationale, closing the gap the validator named (status was never tagged Ecto.Enum or given a values: mapping anywhere in the doc, unlike required_auth/scope in §0's bullet list). Changed every lowercase status-value literal that contradicted the migration to uppercase: §3.1 step 4 (`status = :active` -> `:ACTIVE`), §3.2 step 2/3 (`status == :retired` -> `:RETIRED`, `status = :retired` -> `:RETIRED`, two `status: :retired` prose mentions -> `:RETIRED`), §5 catalog_lookup/1's two `status: :active`/`status: :retired` match descriptions -> `:ACTIVE`/`:RETIRED`. Verified via grep after editing: zero remaining lowercase `:active`/`:retired` status-value atoms in the file (the only remaining lowercase-looking hits are the unrelated field-name atom `:retired_at` and one deliberate 'never use lowercase' clarifying sentence in the new §3.3 subsection). No other section's content touched beyond this reconciliation, per the rework note's explicit instruction -- §1, §2, §4, §6, §7, §8, §9 are byte-identical to the prior iteration. Re-verified branch is feature/WF02-REQ373-20260921 before editing.

Prior-iteration verification (unchanged, not redone per the rework note): Design artefact produced at lib/letflow/design/req373-service-catalog-version-lifecycle.md. Re-read (not trusted from the requirement text) lib/letflow/service_catalog.ex, lib/letflow/service_catalog/entry.ex, lib/letflow/engine/pin_resolver.ex, and lib/letflow/engine.ex's exact pin_lookup/2 call site, plus lib/letflow/routers/admin_services.ex for the existing :AdminServicesManage route convention, and grepped docs/migration/decisions/ for prior versioned-entity precedent (none directly dictates this shape; 0023-entity-storage-hybrid.md's entity_def_version is a different, not-contradicting pattern, cited). SCHEMA DECISION (§1): in-place version/version_id/status/published_at/retired_at columns on service_catalog (representing the single CURRENT version) plus a new sibling table service_catalog_versions archiving every superseded version -- NOT a composite-key (service_id+version) table. Reasoning: PinResolver.Lookup.catalog_lookup/1 itself takes only service_id, never a requested version -- nothing downstream of Lookup ever needs to address a specific historical version by key, so composite-keying buys nothing at the one call site this requirement exists to wire up, while costing a severe, needless blast radius (service_id is used as a bare String.t() key by every existing ServiceCatalog function, by the SERVICE_TASK graph-node reference which has no version concept at all, and by the frozen web/src/api/services.ts wire contract -- REQ-373's own SCOPE FENCE forbids touching the graph layer, which a composite key would require). This choice leaves all five existing public functions (register/1, get_for_tenant/2, list_for_tenant/2, update_scope/2, delete/1) with zero signature/behavior change -- only register/1's insert body gains four additional stamped fields (version='1', ACTIVE, fresh version_id, published_at=now), mirroring how created_at/updated_at are already stamped rather than caller-supplied. AC4's retire-vs-fallback ambiguity is resolved explicitly: retire FAILS OUTRIGHT (reuses the existing {:unresolved_catalog_ref, ref} error, no new error variant) rather than falling through, because the schema enforces at most one ACTIVE row per service_id -- there is structurally no second ACTIVE row to fall through to. The already-pinned-instance half of AC4 is satisfied by construction, not by any code this requirement adds: pin_for/3 is a pure Enum.find/2 over an already-obtained pin list, calls no Lookup and issues no Repo query at all, so retire cannot affect it regardless of what retire does. Every design 'Change' subsection is described in prose (@spec-style signatures + prose behavior), never a literal function body/case-do-end block -- migration and router code was likewise rewritten from Ecto/Phoenix DSL code fences into column/index tables and prose after checking the actual house convention (lib/letflow/design/req191-service-catalog-core.md contains zero code fences for its own migration spec), so as not to repeat the REQ-372 rework precedent (handoffs/WF02-REQ372-20260921/step-01-code-designer.json) of literal .ex code in a design doc. All 8 acceptance criteria are mapped 1:1 to concrete design elements in §8's table. Four open questions listed explicitly (§9): no FK service_catalog_versions->service_catalog to avoid silently changing delete/1's existing error contract (OQ-1, flagged for REVIEWER); no status-based filtering added to the three existing read functions (OQ-2); the publish/retire response JSON's exact key names for the five new fields are left to ELIXIR-DEV, no wire contract exists yet (OQ-3); version strings are treated as fully opaque, no format/ordering constraint (OQ-4).
issues: OQ-1 (design §9): no FK constraint from the new service_catalog_versions table back to service_catalog, specifically to avoid silently giving delete/1 a new FK-violation failure mode it isn't designed to handle and this requirement isn't scoped to change. REVIEWER should confirm this tradeoff (orphaned archive rows after a delete) is acceptable, or direct a follow-up to add ON DELETE CASCADE with delete/1's own contract updated to match.

Design §1 point 2 notes the schema decision deliberately avoids any change to the graph layer (Letflow.Definitions.Graph/PromotionPlan's version-less SERVICE_TASK service_id reference) -- REVIEWER should confirm this reading of the SCOPE FENCE is correct, since it was the deciding factor against the composite-key alternative.

Design §7 route methods (POST for both publish and retire, including retire despite it being a state-transition-only action with no body) and exact path segments (/versions, /retire) are this designer's own naming call, as the task explicitly permitted -- flagged for REVIEWER/ELIXIR-DEV in case a different convention is preferred.
